heading: 2027 City Budget Advances to the Common Council
summary: The Committee of the Whole voted 6–1, with one member not voting, to send the amended 2027 budget to the Common Council. The committee had spent much of its work session debating police camera funding, sustainability staffing and the Media Center. The budget was scheduled for a November 17 public hearing, with further amendments possible at that meeting.

heading: License Plate Reader Funding Survives a 7–1 Vote
summary: The committee voted 7–1 against removing funding for automated license plate readers from the proposed 2027 budget. Public commenters raised concerns about privacy, data sharing and possible misuse, and the police chief said he would make the department’s policy and proposed data-sharing agreement public. Alders also discussed a camera cap and resident oversight as separate policy proposals.

heading: Media Center Staffing Proposal Heads to Council
summary: An amendment would convert two part-time Sun Prairie Media Center jobs to full-time positions using up to $110,000 from the center’s fund balance. The Friends group discussed providing up to $140,000 for programming and equipment, while staff raised concerns about paying recurring salaries from reserves. The committee referred the staffing amendment to the Common Council for further discussion.

heading: Committee Rejects Staffing Swap to Preserve Sustainability Role
summary: Alders voted 6–2 against eliminating a planning support position to fund the sustainability program manager. Planning staff said the proposed cut would shift clerical duties to other employees and leave less time for planning work. A subsequent proposal to eliminate a transportation position received no second.

heading: Cannery Square Grant Application Gets Unanimous Backing
summary: The committee voted 8–0 to advance a state Vibrant Spaces grant application for Cannery Square and Market Street. The proposal would add movable vehicle barriers for street closures, replace an aging speaker system and improve signage for downtown events. The grant would require a city match of up to $50,000, and the application was slated for Common Council review.

heading: Public Works Backs Five-Year Drainage Agreement Renewal
summary: The Public Works Committee backed renewal of the city’s agreement with the Dane County Drainage District under existing terms. Sun Prairie would continue to cover 45% of major work in drainage districts 8 and 9 and contribute to routine maintenance. Staff said the arrangement spreads costs across the city and avoids separate district assessments for affected residents who already pay stormwater utility fees.

heading: Main Street Inspection Extended As Crews Target Thanksgiving Reopening
summary: Engineering staff reported a $48,500 change order to extend construction inspection on the Main Street reconstruction project. The committee chair and city administrator had already approved the change after unexpected conditions and added work extended the schedule. Staff said the goal was to restore two-way traffic by Thanksgiving week and defer plantings until the following year.

heading: Staff Outline 2027 Wastewater and Stormwater Rate Increases
summary: Public Works staff reported planned 2027 rate increases of 9.9% for wastewater and 3.5% for stormwater. A committee member asked about the size of the wastewater increase. Staff pointed to recent wastewater investments and a multiyear utility rate study, and said finance staff had verified both figures.
